rule: A refresh transaction re-reads under the account's store lock, commits a non-secret generation attempt marker before sending, then commits the replacement pair before returning access. A failed attempt-marker save sends nothing. Only a provider refusal (400, 401 or 403, how invalid_grant arrives) marks the generation terminal; only no answer or a server error (5xx) sets it back to ready, so the stored grant is tried again and the sign-in is kept; any other answer, including an accepted 2xx that cannot be read, may have spent the grant and is uncertain. An attempted, uncertain or terminal generation requires sign-in again, even after reconstructing the store or requesting forced refresh. A replacement commit failure never returns the new access token or replays the old grant. A fresh sign-in replaces quarantine. This applies to the TypeScript portable engine, not the frozen Kotlin mirror or the desktop Pi engine.
